name: Huggy Bear
label: Kill Rock Stars
lede: Five people from Brighton promised to last three years, refused the photographs and the interviews, turned down the major labels, and kept every one of those promises.

eras.title: Girl-boy revolutionaries
eras.text: Huggy Bear formed in Brighton in 1991 as a mix of women and men, and called themselves girl-boy revolutionaries. Their first records came out on Wiiija in 1992, and the bidding wars started before the band would talk to anyone.

years.h: Brighton five-piece debuts opening for Heavenly
years.p: Niki Eleni, [[Jo Johnson|5c306572-a722-4e91-bbcf-e93f06cee73e]], Karen Hill, Chris Rowley and [[Jon Slade|c749b05c-ce7a-47ba-bd6b-6d3790c6ec34]] play their first show as support to Heavenly, per AllMusic.
The debut 7-inch on Wiiija, pressed in a limited run of 2,000 copies, mixes shouted punk with tape collage.
years.xp: AllMusic describes the record as musical rants and tape pastiches carrying a political message. Wikipedia lists the 2,000-copy limit for the 7-inch.

years.h: Major labels bid. Huggy Bear stays on Wiiija
years.p: After Wiiija collects early demos, AllMusic reports a major-label bidding war. The band stays independent.
years.xp: The band also declined interviews and photographs for most of its life and kept its full names off the record, according to AllMusic and Wikipedia. It was a house rule, not a stunt for the press to solve.

years.h: Kiss Curl for the Kid's Lib Guerrillas · Wiiija 18
years.p: A second 7-inch on Wiiija closes 1992, three months after the debut.

eras.title: The Word, and everything after
eras.text: 1993 is the year Huggy Bear meets Bikini Kill, plays live network TV and gets dragged out of it. The British music press turns riot grrrl into a story, and the band keeps releasing records anyway.

years.big: Live TV, Valentine's Day, escorted out
years.p: Huggy Bear play "Her Jazz" on Channel 4's The Word, then protest a segment on the Barbi Twins and are ejected.
years.xp: After the performance the band and friends shouted at presenter Terry Christian over the Barbi Twins item, and security removed them. A show spokesperson said someone had bitten the face of a production staffer. John Robb, who was there, disputed that, saying no biting happened and security was heavy-handed. Melody Maker compared the row to the Sex Pistols and Bill Grundy.

years.h: [[Bikini Kill|1397d045-1603-41fc-80b9-712c18360145]] cross the Atlantic and tour with Huggy Bear
years.p: [[Kathleen Hanna|4638653b-a279-42d6-bd8c-b2bcb9a19f77]]'s band joins Huggy Bear on a British tour, a meeting Ngaire Ruth's history of riot grrrl calls pivotal in bringing the scene to Britain.

q: So simple, so ugly, so daring.
years.h: Split with Bikini Kill: Our Troubled Youth
years.p: Released on International Women's Day. Huggy Bear's side comes out on Catcall Records in the UK and Kill Rock Stars in the US; Bikini Kill's is Yeah Yeah Yeah Yeah.
years.xp:
Huggy Bear's side has eight songs, including "Blow Dry", "Hopscotch" and "February 14th". NME's Lisa Wright called it a more perfect teenage punk album you will not find.

Gordon Moakes of Bloc Party later named "Blow Dry" as a formative record for him.

years.h: Taking the Rough with the Smooch collects the early singles
years.p: The compilation on Kill Rock Stars and Wiiija gathers the early recordings for listeners outside the UK.

years.h: Jo and Niki start Blood Sausage with Brighton friends
years.p: [[Blood Sausage|bb52564b-068a-4dda-9214-6429f98e01ff]] is a side project with poet Dale Shaw, and its Touching You in Ways That Don't Feel Comfortable EP is NME Single of the Week.

eras.title: Three years, as promised
eras.text: The band always said it would last three years. In 1994 the line-up drops to four, the only album arrives, and the last show closes the year.

years.p: [[Jon Slade|c749b05c-ce7a-47ba-bd6b-6d3790c6ec34]] leaves in early 1994, per Wikipedia, and later joins [[Comet Gain|65cc77e1-45cf-4c2a-958c-c7cca472970c]].

years.src: Wikipedia: Weaponry Listens to Love · AllMusic
years.h: Weaponry Listens to Love, the only album
years.p: Released on Wiiija in the UK and Kill Rock Stars in the US, with Slade gone: a heavier record, with more male lead vocals than before, per AllMusic.
years.xp: Reviews were mixed. The Guardian said it was as enraged as the first but lacked its modulating whimsy; The Rocket called it brutal, harsh and chilling; NME gave it 6 out of 10. Tracks include "Immature Adolescence" and "Facedown".

years.h: The final show, three years after they started
years.p: Huggy Bear break up in December 1994, keeping a promise to last three years. Wikipedia places the split shortly after a North American tour.

eras.title: Killed (Of Kids)
eras.text: The members go quiet as a band and busy in others. In 2024 a book collects everything they made, and three of them play together for the first time in thirty years.

years.p: With members of Male Bonding, Rowley releases County Pride in 2020 on What's Your Rupture? Karen Hill's [[Phantom Pregnancies|2973b718-e4ec-49ac-b116-9d611a343474]] and Jo Johnson's ambient records are others.

years.h: Killed (Of Kids): all seven zines in one book
years.p: A 352-page book from JABS and The Grass Is Green In The Fields For You holds the band's zines, photos, flyers and new interviews with all five members.
years.xp: At the book launch at New River Studios, Karen Hill, Jon Slade and Chris Rowley performed together for the first time in thirty years, according to Wikipedia.

sources.title: Loud Women: What did riot grrrl ever do for us? Part 2
